newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Platinum metals sharply higher in volatile Europe.
newsitem.headline: Platinum metals sharply higher in volatile Europe.

text.p: Platinum group metals (PGMs) opened sharply higher in Europe as nervousness about when Russian deliveries would start continued to drive prices higher in speculative, volatile trading, dealers said on Wednesday.

"There is a big squeeze in both platinum and palladium. Even though we heard yesterday a Russian delegation was in Japan, the speculative dealing continued. I can't say how things are going to go now," one analyst at a leading Swiss bank said.
"The higher they go the lower they will fall when news comes of the first Russian deliveries," he added, forecasting another volatile day.
Platinum started at $425.00/$435.00 an ounce, up from $415.00/$419.00 at Tuesday's London close. It eased in early business as bid/offer spreads remained wide.
Palladium advanced to $212.00/$222.00 from $193.00/$197.00. It also slipped in early business.
"Much more is being traded than is physically available," one trader said.
Gold opened firmer but within its previous range, little moved by the apparent agreement between the Bonn government and the Bundesbank over German plans to revalue gold reserves.
Silver moved up four cents an ounce to $4.77/$4.79 in line with gold.
